title: City breathing: Milan's daily NO2 pulse

link.method: Pearson r, hourly Milan NO2 (EEA, mean of stations) vs ERA5 Milan 10 m wind speed, daily cycle removed from both (mean of each hour of day subtracted), lags -12..12 h
link.partner_choice: wind: it is the physical driver (dilution) of the Milan NO2 swings; Paris shares the human rhythm but not the weather, so Milan vs Paris is reported only as a comparison

gaps: Station hours flagged invalid by the agencies are empty and stay empty; a city lane is empty in any hour where fewer than half of its stations report.
Stations kept only with at least 80% valid hours in the 4 weeks.
EEA times are taken as the station time zone (UTC+01, no daylight saving), which is local time in January and February.
Wind is ERA5 reanalysis (a model) at about 25 km, read at points from the Open-Meteo archive; streaks are 3-hourly on a 1 degree grid.
Both NO2 and wind have a daily rhythm (traffic and the night inversion), so the raw hourly correlation partly reflects the clock; the headline link removes the mean daily cycle from both.
Paris has no 2019 holiday in this window either; its lane is a comparison, not a partner of Milan.

hero_norm.method: min..max of the hero series itself (Milan hourly NO2, mean of stations), 4 weeks

sources.name: EEA air quality e-reporting, verified hourly NO2 (E1a), Milan
sources.producer: European Environment Agency, data from ARPA Lombardia via ISPRA

sources.producer: European Environment Agency, data from Airparif via LCSQA
